content.text:
**Finding submitted: deviation (high severity).**

Contrary to the planner's expectation that no customer-payable damages existed, Section 4.2 contains a **Termination Payment** payable by the Company (Deerskin) to HDI: one-half of the prior twelve months' Net Sales above $800,000, paid in eight quarterly instalments.

Why it fails the fallback:
- Fees under Section 3.1 are only 30% of monthly Net Sales above $11,000. The Termination Payment overtakes three months' fees once annual Net Sales exceed roughly $918k, and at $2m of Net Sales it is over a year's worth of fees.
- Section 4.1 allows either party to terminate on 90 days' notice, so the remaining contract value at termination is small — the payment can exceed it, edging into walk-away territory.
- It bites on *any* Company termination, including termination for HDI's own breach.

Redline (validated, ok:true): a proviso capping the Termination Payment at three times the average monthly Section 3.1 payment over the preceding twelve months — the playbook fallback — with outright deletion offered as our preferred alternative in the comment.
